description_en: This three-bayphalcāis located at Calakhu Square. A stone inscription attests to its original construction in 1775. Sadly, little of its original structure remains, with the exception of six original columns, complete with their plates and capitals. Following the 1934 CE earthquake, the roof was replaced with a concrete slab and a brick balustrade featuring ornamental plaster. Thephalcāwas severely damaged in the 2015 earthquakes. In ca. 2020, emergency repairs were carried out that included the replacement of the balustrade with an unsightly brick and cement wall and the replacement of two beams with pine timber.In circa the 1920s, a Śākya family purchased the house behind thephalcā. According to locals, rituals are no longer performed at the site. Nevertheless, travelers still use it as a resting place, and vendors sell vegetables there daily
description_ne: तीन वटा कवल भएको यो फल्चा उन्नाईसौँ शताब्दीको मध्यतिर पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको जस्तो देखिन्छ । त्यति वेलाका ६ वटा काष्ठस्तम्भ र दलिन अहिले पनि सुरक्षित देखिन्छन् । पुरानो छाना झिकेर नयाँ बार्दली हालिएको छ, तर यो काम कहिले भयो थाहा छैन । फल्चाभन्दा पछाडिको घर सन् १९२० तिर शाक्य परिवारले किनेका थिए । स्थानीयले दिएको जानकारी अनुसार फल्चामा धार्मिक सांस्कृतिक गतिविधि भएको देखिँदैन तर कहिलेकाहीँ बटुवाहरू भने यहाँ सुत्ने गर्दछन् । फल्चामा दैनिक तर्कारी किनबेच भएको देखिन्छ ।
brick_type: desi apā (modern brick), mā apā (regular fired brick), dāci apā (conical veneer brick)
monument_assessment: Heavily damaged (collapsed, demolished, major cracks and structural damages)
references: Sources and references Inscription identification number LAL4224_I_001 Sources Stone stele inscription embedded in a niche in the phalcā's wall. H: 30 cm, W: 24 cm Details Stone inscription of Calakhu phalcā related to Nārāyaṇa (transliteration and translation by Nutan Sharma, 2018) oṃ namaḥ nārāyaṇaṃ namaskṛtyaṃ naraṃ cau(cai)va narottamāṃ(mam) devīṃ saraś(s)vatīṃ (vyāsaṃ) ta- to jaya mut(d)īraya(e)[t] ||  || śreyostu || saṃmvat 895 māghakṛṣṇa || ṣaṣṭhān tithau bṛhaspativāsare thva kunhu kutubāhālayā laghuvaṃśa rāutta  si _ _ ... ... sa_ siddhilakṣmimaī thva nimha stri pu[ru]khasena svapurta divaṃgata _ _ datta bābusa māmana calaṣu lāṃche͂sa phale dayakaṃ śrī nārāyaṇa mūrtti _ _ _ _ pratiṣṭhā yāsyaṃ śrī 3 candamāsasa duntā pākubuṃ rova 3 java 3 _tasiṃdhuṣacābuṃ rova 3 puna dhalasikva karṣa 7 thvate buṃyā _ _ syanana _ phalesa mata choyakaṃ dāna biyamāla buṃgayātāna enātava || ni... ... _ _bhāropanisena yāyamāla saeva vaiśāṣa lachiṃ śrī 3 buṃga yāta ... ... ... ... || śrī _ _ 2 vaṃ _ _ tya japa pāṭha rācake || śrī 3 bo _ śvara ... ... ... ... kārttika lachiṃ mata biyake māla ... ... ... ... varṣaprati ... ... ... ... yāyamāla  cosye tako yātasā utrottara juya || cosya (tako) mayātasā paṃcamāhāpāpa lāka || śubhamastu || Translation of the inscription: (The beginning part of the inscription is the praises of Lord Narayan) In [NS] 895 (1775 CE), on the 6th day of dark half of Lunar month of Māgha, Thrusday. On this day, the couple from Kutu Bāhā, Si... ... Raghuvaṃśa Rāutta and his wife Siddhilakṣīmayī. The mother of the dead son has constructed this phalcā of Calkhu, Lāṃche͂ establishing in it an icon of Śrīnārāyaṇa in the name of the dead son ... Datta Bābu. Three ropani and 3 yava land of Pākubuṃ, 3 ropani s of land of Tasiṃ Dhuṣacābuṃ and 7 karṣa of land of Dholosikvaṃ are offered.  Those lands shall be used to repair the phalcā when destroyed. Burning lamps shall be offered there during the festival of red Matsyendranātha.... The Bhāro (noble) brothers shall do this during the whole month of Vaiśakha during the festival of red Matsyendranātha .... [Also,] japa (recitation of mantra ) and pāṭha (recitation of sacred texts) shall also be performed.... A lamp shall be offered in the whole month of Kārtika.... Every year.... If done according to what has been written, he shall get prosperous and if not done he shall get five great sins .... May all be well.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of the phalcā and donation of land
historical_events.event_description: According to the inscription, thephalcāwas built by a couple from Kutu Bāhāḥ in the name of their late son and is dedicated to Śrīnārāyaṇa. Locals say that the statue said to have been installed at the time of construction has since been lost. Threeropaniand 3yavaland of Pākubuṃ, 3ropanis of land of Tasiṃ Dhuṣacābuṃ and 7 karṣa of land of Dholosikvaṃ are offered.The inscription prescribes that the Bhāro (noble) brothers must offer burning wick lamps to the deity of thephalcāduring the entire month of Vaiśākha, including during the festival of the Rato (Red) Matsyendranātha. Moreover,japa(mantra)andpāṭha(sacred texts) shall be recited at this time. A lamp shall be offered for the whole month of Kārtika. Nowadays, these rituals are no longer performed.
